So, I have been screwing around with paper patching for the Mosin Nagant using the Lee tl230-5r. Thats right, the 300 BLK mold. The boolit requires sizing down to .305 from .310 which takes two steps. As you might imagine, the process takes a lot of lube, and being as they are Lee tl bullets, I used liquid Alox. Well, I though I could just leave the alox on the bullet after I wrapped the paper on. Big Mistake. I think the lube was sticky enough to carry the patch with it to the target on slower loads, resulting in 6-8" groups. But once I cranked the speed up, accuracy just went to hell. I think that with the higher speed was enough to start to strip the patch with wind resistance before reaching the target.

So, to remedy this, I will be removing the Alox with acetone. Already have some loaded for next weekend. Wish me luck.

P.S. I'm estimating starting load speed to be 1700 fps, and final load to be around 2200, when I start to get the accuracy I want, I will crony.
